provenance: Algospeak — vocabulary that exists specifically to evade automated moderation — plus the signalling conventions of the adult creator economy. This is the register's most practically useful function: it is what trust-and-safety systems, platform researchers and worried parents actually need decoded, and it is deliberately designed to be illegible to keyword filters. Coverage here was previously a single entry (🌽). Descriptive reference only; gated by default.

🌶️.gloss: The dominant euphemism for adult material across TikTok and Instagram. 'Spicy accounts', 'spicy content', 'my spicy link' — chosen because the word is innocuous enough to survive keyword filtering while being universally understood.

🔞.gloss: The literal Unicode meaning ('no one under eighteen'), used as a self-applied content label rather than a prohibition.

🅾️.gloss: Platform names are themselves filtered, so they get spelled with lookalike glyphs. The O button is the common first letter.

🎂.gloss: Used in bios to assert being over eighteen, both sincerely and as a fig leaf.

💰.gloss: Marks material behind a paywall or a tip request.

💳.gloss: The transactional half of the creator-economy signal set.

🔒.gloss: Widely used in creator posts to mark a preview; distinct from the security-fix and chastity senses recorded elsewhere.

🤫.gloss: Signals privacy expectations in solicitation and affair-adjacent messaging.

📩.gloss: Moves a transaction off a public timeline where it would be moderated.

🍬.gloss: 'Sugar' relationships, in the sugar-baby / sugar-daddy sense. A sweetness pun rather than a shape one.

🍯.gloss: Interchangeable with 🍬 in that construction, alongside its endearment sense.

🐰.gloss: The bunny as an adult-industry visual shorthand, distinct from its Korean-fandom and Mandarin-cute readings.

👑.gloss: Two adjacent readings: a hierarchy claim in kink contexts, and a creator-ranking badge in adult platforms.

🌽.gloss: 'Corn' as a deliberate misspelling of 'porn', the single most cited algospeak example. Originated on TikTok specifically to survive keyword moderation, and now widely understood outside it.

🥞.gloss: Part of the broader pattern where innocuous food glyphs stand in for filtered words; the specific mapping shifts as filters adapt.

👻.gloss: Points at a platform with weaker moderation and disappearing media, rather than referring to ghosting.

📸.gloss: In creator bios, an offer rather than a hobby; in dating, a verification request.

💸.gloss: Payment as part of the interaction itself, common in findom contexts.

⭐.gloss: Marks a paid or higher tier in creator-account menus.
